iut_type: End Product (Yaman product, module-based), whether Bluetooth registration is required when the product doesn't display the Bluetooth logo
customer_question: Our product doesn't display the Bluetooth logo, so do we still need to register it with Bluetooth SIG and pay the associated fee?
question_variants: Is module-level QDID certification (purchased from our module vendor) sufficient on its own, without our own product-level registration?
Where is it officially documented that registration is required regardless of logo use?
actual_issue: The customer needed to confirm whether the legal/contractual obligation to register a Bluetooth-enabled product with Bluetooth SIG (and pay the Declaration fee) applies even when the finished product does not display the Bluetooth logo at all, and whether their module vendor's own QDID certification was sufficient on its own.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth product registration (obtaining a Declaration ID) is required at the final-product level any time a Bluetooth-enabled product is brought to market under a company's own brand, regardless of whether the Bluetooth logo is actually displayed on the product or its packaging -- the module vendor's own QDID certification covers only the module itself and does not substitute for the final product's own registration. This obligation, and its independence from logo display, is explicitly documented on Bluetooth SIG's own Help & Support page under the heading 'Do I Need to Qualify?,' which the customer can reference directly as the authoritative source. The required payment is the Declaration fee ($11,040 to Bluetooth SIG), which is separate from -- and in addition to -- the proxy registration support and Compliance Folder service fees a consulting firm would charge.
consultant_answer: Yes, registration is required regardless of whether you display the Bluetooth logo -- any Bluetooth-enabled product brought to market under your own brand needs its own product-level registration (Declaration ID), separate from your module vendor's own QDID certification, which only covers the module itself. This requirement, independent of logo display, is documented directly on Bluetooth SIG's Help & Support page under 'Do I Need to Qualify?' -- I'd recommend referencing that page directly. The required Declaration fee is $11,040 to Bluetooth SIG, on top of our proxy registration support and Compliance Folder fees.
decision_logic: Bluetooth product registration obligation is triggered by bringing a Bluetooth-enabled product to market under one's own brand, not by whether the Bluetooth logo is displayed -- a module vendor's own component-level QDID certification does not substitute for the final product's own required registration, and this distinction should be explained with reference to Bluetooth SIG's own official documentation rather than asserted without a citable source.
final_recommendation: When a customer asks whether registration is needed despite not using the Bluetooth logo, cite Bluetooth SIG's own 'Do I Need to Qualify?' Help & Support page directly as the authoritative source, rather than simply asserting the requirement, since customers (and their own internal stakeholders) are more likely to accept and act on an officially-documented answer.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer mistakenly believing that avoiding the Bluetooth logo exempts them from registration could face compliance warnings or enforcement action from Bluetooth SIG later, as appears to have happened in a comparable case (see thread_0038).
